blocks.text: Appraisers score **only** with the approved appraisal handbook and instruments. Teaching & Learning documents may clarify good practice, but they **do not replace, expand or create appraisal indicators** — and toolkit habits must never become unofficial appraisal criteria.

chapters.title: Plan the learning, create the environment
chapters.lede: Two documents set the network minimum for every classroom. Both are a common language, not a script — teachers adapt the format to their subject and students.

blocks.title: A lesson plan — the 14 minimum components
blocks.lead: A strong plan makes the learning journey visible: what students will learn, how, how the teacher checks understanding, and what happens next.
points: **Set-up:** class and lesson information · curriculum reference · learning objective(s) · success criteria · prior learning
**The lesson:** opening · teaching and learning sequence · timing · grouping / participation mode
**For every learner:** differentiation and learner support · resources and materials
**Learning made visible:** checks for understanding · closure / consolidation · teacher reflection and next steps
check: The minimum required components are
Checks for understanding / formative assessment
Teacher reflection and next steps

blocks.title: Responding to behaviour — the least disruptive response that works

steps.title: Notice & cue
steps.text: Eye contact, proximity, a pause or gesture.

steps.title: Brief reminder
steps.text: State the expected behaviour calmly and specifically.

steps.title: Private redirection
steps.text: Speak briefly and privately — no public argument.

steps.title: Choice or consequence
steps.text: Use the school's approved structure; no negotiating mid-lesson.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.text: Once calm: what happened, what changes, how to rejoin.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.text: Repeated, serious, unsafe or safeguarding concerns go through the school system.

check: Use the least disruptive effective response and remain within school policy
Refer repeated, serious, unsafe, or safeguarding-related concerns through the school's approved system

blocks.title: In every classroom
do: A clear start, clear instructions and efficient transitions.
Structured pair and group work with active teacher monitoring.
Calm correction, and a deliberate lesson closure.
dont: Public humiliation, sarcasm or personal labels.
Long arguments in front of the class.
Whole-class punishment for one student's behaviour (unless a specific justified procedure exists).
Ignoring serious safety or safeguarding concerns.
check: Sarcasm or personal labels
Whole-class punishment for one student
